title: Farls da bag · modern, image-led home page
question: Modern broadcast, real team images, and less text. Choose the direction to carry forward.

options.label: History on demand
options.thesis: Logo-led record stories make the archive feel ready to explore.
options.viewport: A real team logo anchors the first record story, a second story follows, and record-book access stays visible.
options.risk: Story artwork must stay recognizably tied to a real team rather than become a generic thumbnail.

raised.raise: Give each exhibit a distinct visual identity without burying its name.
Let actual team artwork supply personality while labels remain readable.
Use one confident color field and keep supporting records calm.
Make the season and metric visible with very little text.
Keep source details directly accessible from every highlighted value.
Every story has a clear link and a predictable route back.

options.label: On-air now
options.thesis: Big team identities and precise record graphics replace metallic broadcast chrome.
options.viewport: The Monkey Buccaneers logo carries the lead record, with a lighter second feature and compact exhibit navigation.
options.risk: The familiar sports language needs strong team imagery to feel specific to this league.

options.label: Window-box shelf
options.thesis: Each record is a logo-led collectible box that opens its evidence.
options.viewport: Logo windows occupy a shelf of record exhibits.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity against the requested modern broadcast direction.
options.risk: Box packaging adds decorative layers around simple evidence.

options.label: Blackbook page
options.thesis: Team marks connect the league's history through letterform routes.
options.viewport: Team identity becomes the first record's large visual anchor.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity; letterform navigation fights readable broadcast presentation.
options.kept: Team artwork as the source of personality.
options.risk: Lettering can obscure team and exhibit names.

options.label: Cyclorama
options.thesis: Record stories occupy successive bands of colored stage light.
options.viewport: An illuminated team logo leads into bands of record evidence.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity; atmospheric phases add a metaphor the archive does not need.
options.kept: One strong focal field with calm supporting content.
options.risk: Lighting phases could imply unsupported progress or rankings.

options.label: Brine calendar
options.thesis: Season records line up as dated vessels of preserved history.
options.viewport: Team logos identify dated season collections.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity; jars and preservation read as food rather than football.
options.kept: Compact, visible season and metric labels.
options.risk: The physical metaphor adds bulk and text.

options.label: Oscilloscope
options.thesis: Selected record histories share one measured trace field.
options.viewport: Team channels expose time-series results and their sources.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity; retro instrumentation repeats the dated impression.
options.kept: Exact source access from a highlighted result.
options.risk: Data traces would make a sparse home page feel analytical and dense.

options.label: HyperCard
options.thesis: A stack of addressable record stories preserves a visitor's trail.
options.viewport: One team-led record opens its supporting history.
options.case: Loses audience identification and product clarity; monochrome retro controls contradict the requested modernity.
options.kept: Direct story links and predictable return navigation.
options.risk: Retro interface controls would dominate contemporary team images.

canonCard.label: The familiar sports app
canonCard.thesis: A clean sports archive centered on team avatars and concise record cards.
canonCard.viewport: Two image-led record cards lead into the archive and current-season history.
canonCard.risk: A familiar layout puts most of the identity burden on the team images.
